This review highlights the role of hygroscopic chromium salts in destabilizing the passive film of 316 L and increasing susceptibility to pitting and stress corrosion cracking in chloride media, emphasizing the need for further investigation to better assess corrosion risks in industrial environments.

title: Study on the Influence of Soil Moisture Content and Particle Size on Corrosion Behavior of X80 Steel Under Metro Stray Current Interference
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic stray currents generated during subway operations induce corrosion on adjacent buried steel oil and gas pipelines, with their corrosion behavior closely tied to the surrounding soil environment. This study focused on X80 pipeline steel and investigated the influence of two typical parameters—soil moisture content (10%, 20%, and 30%) and soil particle size (100, 500, and 1000 μm) on X80 steel corrosion behavior. Electrochemical testing, corrosion weight loss analysis, and morphological analysis were employed to investigate the relationship between varying corrosion patterns and soil conditions. The results demonstrate a strong positive correlation between soil moisture content and the corrosion rate of X80 steel. The corrosion rate of X80 steel showed a strong positive correlation with soil moisture content. This trend is primarily due to the role of water in enhancing the continuity and ionic conductivity of the soil electrolyte, which facilitates charge transfer and accelerates anodic dissolution. Electrochemical analysis revealed that under high moisture conditions, the film resistance ( R f ) of corrosion products decreased significantly, indicating increased corrosion current and accelerated corrosion rates. In contrast, larger soil particle sizes inhibited corrosion progression. Coarse‐grained soil (1000 μm), characterized by higher porosity, impeded the transport of water and oxygen, leading to increased ( R f ) and charge transfer resistance. This resulted in fewer pits and shallower corrosion depths. Cathodic protection potential also significantly influences corrosion behavior. A potential of −1.2 V SCE more effectively suppresses corrosion than −1.1 V SCE . This study clarifies the interactions among dynamic stray currents, soil media, and cathodic protection, offering theoretical and practical insights for corrosion risk assessment and protection for buried pipelines near subway systems.

title: Self‐Healing Corrosion Inhibition of Epoxy Polymer Composite Coatings Using Corrosion Inhibitor and Water‐Dispersed Nanoparticles
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymer composite coatings were fabricated using water‐dispersed nanoparticles and corrosion inhibitor. Carbon steel substrates were coated with a mixture of solvent‐based epoxy resin, water‐dispersed silica nanoparticles (NPs) with diameters from 45 to 180 nm, and magnesium phosphate powder (MP) particles with an average diameter of 1 µm. The coating containing 4 wt% NPs exhibited a resistance of more than 1200 Ω cm 2 after 24 h of immersion into a NaCl solution, which was approximately twice that of the NP‐free coating. The incorporation of larger NPs resulted in a resistance of 2200 Ω cm 2 after 24 h, representing the highest polarization resistance achieved in this study. This work is an investigation into the role of NPs and water within a polymer matrix. The NPs were preferentially distributed around the MP particles. In addition, the polymer coating containing 4 wt% water‐dispersed NPs showed lower levels of water uptake compared with that of the NP‐free coating. The self‐healing corrosion inhibition performance of the composite coating is attributed to the sustained release of corrosion inhibitor through uniformly distributed pores within the polymer matrix.

title: Ni‐Co‐WC Composite Coatings Prepared by Magnetic Field Assisted Jet Electrodeposition: Effects of Magnetic Field Intensity and WC Concentration on Microstructure and Properties
abstract: ABSTRACT Ni‐Co alloy‐based composite coatings have gained substantial research interest in surface engineering owing to their superior mechanical and anti‐corrosion properties. In this study, Ni‐Co‐WC composite coatings were successfully prepared through a novel magnetic field‐assisted jet electrodeposition process. The investigation systematically explored the influence of WC particle dosage in the plating bath and magnetic field intensity upon the surface topography, grain refinement, microhardness, and anti‐corrosion performance of the coatings. The experimental findings demonstrated that appropriately selected WC concentration and magnetic field intensity could synergistically enhance the overall performance of the coatings. With a WC concentration of 10 g/L and a magnetic field intensity of 0.4 T, the resulting coating exhibited the highest WC co‐deposition efficiency, with grains refined to approximately 13.7 nm and a smooth, compact, and defect‐free surface morphology. The optimized coating displayed exceptional comprehensive mechanical and corrosive properties, achieving a maximum microhardness of 617 HV and a minimum of corrosion current density of 0.016 μA·cm⁻².

title: Corrosion Inhibition Behavior of Aluminum Alloy by EDTA Sodium Salts in Simulated HVDC Internal Cooling Water
abstract: ABSTRACT Aluminum radiators in converter valve systems of high‐voltage direct current (HVDC) transmissions are prone to corrosion under the coupled effects of multiple physical fields. The resulting Al 3+ deposit on the grading electrode surface can lead to serious safety incidents. In this study, ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid disodium (EDTA‐2Na), trisodium (EDTA‐3Na), and tetrasodium (EDTA‐4Na) salts are employed as corrosion inhibitors, and 10 mM HCl is used to simulate the acidic environment formed on aluminum radiator surfaces under high electric potential. The corrosion inhibition behavior of aluminum in the electrolyte was systematically investigated. The results showed that the inhibition efficiencies of 5 mM EDTA‐2Na, 3 mM EDTA‐3Na, and 1 mM EDTA‐4Na reached 99.09%, 99.10%, and 98.70%, respectively. The differences in inhibition performance were mainly attributed to variations in solution pH induced by different numbers of sodium ions, which altered the predominant EDTA species in solution. Furthermore, the adsorption configurations of the inhibitors on the aluminum surface were analyzed using physical characterization techniques and theoretical calculations.

title: Corrosion Behavior and Mechanism of Spark Plasma Sintered and Arc‐Melted MoNbTaW Refractory High‐Entropy Alloys in Molten Cerium
abstract: ABSTRACT Refractory high‐entropy alloys (RHEAs) show promising prospects in nuclear applications due to outstanding radiation tolerance, mechanical performance and corrosion resistance. In this study, MoNbTaW RHEA was synthesized via spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 2200°C, while the alloy with identical composition prepared via arc melting served as the control. The two alloys were first systematically characterized for microstructure, densification, grain size and phase constitution, followed by static immersion corrosion testing in molten cerium at 1400°C for 10 h, as well as systematic testing of their room‐temperature mechanical properties. The results reveal that Ta and W possess higher corrosion resistance than Mo and Nb. Benefiting from refined grains and homogeneous microstructure, the SPS alloy achieves better corrosion resistance and mechanical performance, with a mass loss rate of 3.57%, a corrosion rate of 2.72 μm/h, a Vickers hardness of 570.8 HV and a compressive strength of 2585 MPa.

title: Fracture of the Passive Film on Reinforcing Steel in Concrete Under Mechanical Loading
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the fracture of the passive film on reinforcing steel when steel elongation exceeds a threshold value, in the absence of aggressive species such as chlorides or carbon dioxide. Reinforced concrete specimens are subjected to three‐point bending to generate a load‐induced crack. Steel coupons embedded in the concrete are electrically connected to the reinforcing steel to measure the macro cell corrosion current when an anodic site forms. Once the critical load for concrete cracking is exceeded, a macro cell corrosion current is recorded as soon as the load increases, indicating rupture of the passive film and, consequently, anodic activity at the crack location, associated with the formation of a new passive film that heals the passive film fracture. The elongation threshold is close to 950 microstrain (or 190 MPa). As soon as the load stops increasing, the corrosion current sharply decreases, suggesting rapid repair of the passive film. After this repair, small variations in the tensile stress of the reinforcement lead to measurable corrosion currents, indicating that the repaired zone may constitute a weak point in the passive film.

title: Cover Picture: Materials and Corrosion. 6/2026
abstract: Cover: Corrosion morphology and pit depth of CFRP and Q235 samples under different coupling conditions observed by CLSM. According to the 3D corrosion images and the corresponding pit depth measurements, the pits on the Q235 carbon steel surface after coupling were deeper than those of the uncoupled samples, and the corrosion pits on the uncoupled sample surface were longer in diameter and shallower in corrosio. The pitting depth on the CFRP surface after coupling was shallower than that of the uncoupled sample, indicating that the galvanic effect accelerated the corrosion of the anodic Q235 carbon steel, while protecting the cathodic CFRP from corrosion degradation. More detailed information can be found in: Yue Hou, Zihao Guo,Tao Li, Xiaopeng Cheng, Shougang Chen, Exploring Galvanic Corrosion Behavior of CFRP/Q235 Carbon Steel in Marine Environment, Materials and Corrosion 2026, 77, 874.

title: Atmospheric Corrosion Protection of LPBF Manufactured AlSi10Mg by Combining SiO x ‐CVD and PDMS Grafting
abstract: ABSTRACT Additive manufacturing by laser powder bed fusion enables complex AlSi10Mg components but produces a heterogeneous microstructure prone to localized corrosion. In this study, hydrophobic polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) ultrathin films, with and without an SiO ₓ interlayer attached by chemical vapor deposition (CVD), were applied for corrosion mitigation. Surface modifications were characterized by X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), polarization modulation–infrared reflection–absorption spectroscopy (PM‐IRRAS) and water contact angle (WCA) measurements. Electrochemical behavior was evaluated by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), linear sweep voltammetry (LSV), and chronoamperometry by a droplet‐cell approach. Atmospheric corrosion processes simulating marine corrosion were monitored by optical microscopy. Spectroscopic analyses confirm successful PDMS attachment. Electrochemical measurements reveal reduced corrosion current densities by one magnitude, suppressed pitting activity, and anodic shifts of the pitting potential. The SiO ₓ ‐CVD + PDMS bilayer exhibits the highest resistance to atmospheric corrosion.

title: Failure Analysis and Stress Corrosion Cracking Mechanism of UNS N08825 Hydraulic Control Lines in Heavy Oil Thermal Recovery Wells
abstract: ABSTRACT Corrosion cracking occurred in UNS N08825 hydraulic control lines during heavy oil thermal recovery at 350°C. In this study, failure analysis was conducted through fracture surface analysis, crack metallographic analysis, material property testing, and failure reproduction tests. Based on SEM images of the fracture and metallographic images of the cracks, it was found that the cracks in the hydraulic control line initiated from the outer surface of the pipe wall and propagated toward the inner wall in a dendritic morphology until fracture, with the fracture surface exhibiting brittle fracture characteristics. Based on fractography and crack analysis, the failure was identified as stress corrosion cracking (SCC). Corrosion tests were performed to reproduce and verify the failure mechanism. The corrosion tests further elucidated the role of oxygen in SCC, demonstrating that oxygen synergistically accelerates pitting with chloride ions, facilitates hydrogen sulfide penetration into the grain interior, and ultimately leads to SCC under applied stress.

title: Relationship Between the Ferrite/Austenite Ratio and Pitting Corrosion Resistance of 2507 Super Duplex Stainless Steel Produced by the LP‐DED Process
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, the pitting corrosion behavior of 2507 super duplex stainless steel (SDSS) produced by the laser powder‐directed energy deposition (LP‐DED) process was investigated in both as‐built and heat treated (HT) conditions. Compared with the wrought SDSS and HT LP‐DED SDSS, the as‐built LP‐DED SDSS exhibits an increase in the ferrite content of approximately 75%. For HT LP‐DED SDSS specimens, potentiodynamic polarization tests revealed that the pitting potential decreased with increasing heat treatment temperature. The Pitting Resistance Equivalent Number (PREN) was calculated for each phase in each material examined in this study to elucidate the relationship between microstructure and pitting corrosion resistance.

title: Enhancing the Corrosion Resistance Profile of Zirconium‐Based Amorphous Alloy Through Oxygen Ion Implantation
abstract: ABSTRACT The corrosion is one of the prime factors responsible for losses/degradations occurring in the materials. The zirconium‐based amorphous alloys were investigated for assessing their robustness against corrosion. Corrosion behavior under pristine and oxygen‐implanted conditions was compared in three acidic media. To study the effect of fluence on corrosion resistance, implantation was performed at three fluence rates, with the highest fluence (3 × 10 17 ions/cm 2 ) showing the best corrosion resistance. The appearance of crystalline phases subjected to the oxygen ion implantation was identified and verified using grazing incidence X‐ray diffraction (GIXRD), field‐emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) micrographs, and X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). Quantitative EDS analysis indicated a systematic increase in surface oxygen concentration from 0 at.% to 31.18 at.% with increasing fluence. Oxygen implantation at 3 × 10 17 ions/cm 2 resulted in a significant reduction in corrosion current density (I corr ). It is believed that the study paves the way towards improving the corrosion resistance of amorphous alloys by means of the implantation method.

title: Corrosion‐Protection of T122 Steel Using g‐C <sub>3</sub> N <sub>5</sub> ‐Embedded Epoxy Coatings
abstract: ABSTRACT Corrosion‐protection performance of a polymeric coating composed of g‐C 3 N 5 (CN) combined with epoxy (EP) on a T122 steel is systematically evaluated in two corrosive environments i.e., 3.5% NaCl and 0.1 M H 2 SO 4 . The electrochemical corrosion experiments suggest that the g‐C 3 N 5 concentration significantly affects the performance of EP towards the corrosion protection. The composite of EP containing 2% g‐C 3 N 5 (TEP2CN) exhibited the highest polarization/noise resistance values ( R p and R n , respectively) and showed the best performance against corrosion. This is mostly attributed to the blockage of the pores in the EP by the low quantity of added g‐C 3 N 5 which subsequently prohibits the ionic diffusion to the T122 steel surface. However, upon increasing the g‐C 3 N 5 ‐content to 5% (in TEP5CN), the protection performance degrades significantly because in this case, the coating partially delaminates facilitating the passage of the corrosive ions to diffuse through the coating to the T122 steel. The obtained electrochemical results suggest that the CN, when embedded in optimized quantity, can significantly improve the corrosion resistance of epoxy‐based coatings.

title: Assessment of Electrical Resistance Sensors Sensitivity to Localized Corrosion
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper investigates the sensitivity of electrical resistance (ER) sensors to localized corrosion. Analytical models were developed to simulate the ER sensor response to various geometries of localized attacks. These theoretical predictions were validated against experimental data, including controlled electrochemical dissolution and realistic sodium chloride exposure. The comparison revealed a strong correlation between the models and experimental measurements, highlighting a critical limitation of the resistometric method: ER sensors severely underestimate the actual depth of localized attacks. Specifically, models demonstrate that for a localized attack covering less than 5% of the sensor's measuring area, a defect consuming 80% of the initial thickness yields an apparent overall sensor reading of merely 20% thickness loss. Furthermore, under practical NaCl exposure scenarios, actual pit depths reaching 50 µm resulted in sensor readings of only 11 µm. These findings are essential for the accurate interpretation of ER sensor data and the implementation of appropriate safety margins in industrial applications.

title: Nature of Surface Microcracks on Phosphorus Micro‐Alloyed Copper
abstract: ABSTRACT The effect of plastic deformation and environment on the appearance of surface microcracks on phosphorus micro‐alloyed copper (Cu‐OFP) was studied by tensile test, scanning electron microscopy and focused ion beam milling (SEM‐FIB). Specimens tested in ambient conditions under tensile loading showed several thousand microcracks per mm 2 , with maximum length in the range of 15–20 µm and maximum depth of about 3 µm. Increasing plastic deformation resulted in a larger number of microcracks. While specimens tested in water with 80 mg/L sulfide showed a much smaller microcrack density, with no indication of growth due to the presence of sulfides. Tensile testing of three different batches of Cu‐OFP material showed similar results, suggesting that the results are batch‐independent. These results indicate that surface microcracks form on Cu‐OFP due to plastic straining both in air and in sulfide‐containing water. Furthermore, this study demonstrates that, under the tested conditions, sulfide exposure does not promote microcrack propagation through stress corrosion cracking.

title: Environment Stewardship Using Mangifera indica Kernel's Biochar Incorporated CeO 2 Nanotubes Loaded With Self‐Healing Benzotriazole as Corrosion Resistant Coatings to Extend the Life of Mild Steel Meant for Industrial Aqueous Medium
abstract: ABSTRACT In this investigative study, a fresh amalgamated composite coating BTA@MBCENT (benzotriazole or BTA‐loaded mango kernel biochar or MB incorporated CeO 2 nanotubes, abbreviated as CENT) with varying weight percentages in epoxy resin is prepared and applied to cherish the environment for industries using mild steel, specifically using saline water (3.5% sodium chloride) circulation systems. The novel coating MBCENT was then employed to examine its life‐lengthening and self‐healing properties against corrosion, a priori and a posteriori incorporating BTA. After completing the necessary characterization, the coating formulations applied over mild steel surfaces exhibited a water‐repellent property. The release kinetics of self‐healing BTA inhibitor were evaluated using ultraviolet spectroscopy. Protection efficacy for the coated steel samples immersed is investigated through electrochemical methods. BTA@MBCENT (1.0%) demonstrated an exceptional protection efficiency of 88.63% within 42 days of immersion, suggesting the self‐healing coating may serve as a viable alternative to conventional anticorrosive coatings for mild steel against aggressive chloride ions of saline industrial water.

title: Tribological Behavior and Lead‐Bismuth Eutectic Corrosion Resistance of a Laser‐Cladding Fe <sub>47.0</sub> Cr <sub>24.1</sub> Mo <sub>6.0</sub> Nb <sub>2.9</sub> Ni <sub>15.0</sub> Al <sub>5.0</sub> High‐Entropy Alloy Coating
abstract: ABSTRACT A Fe 47.0 Cr 24.1 Mo 6.0 Nb 2.9 Ni 15.0 Al 5.0 high‐entropy alloy (HEA) coating containing Laves and B2‐NiAl phases was fabricated on 304 stainless steel substrates by laser cladding. Compared with the substrate, the coating exhibited increases of 88% in hardness and 75% in wear resistance by dry sliding tests in air at room temperature, 350°C, and 550°C for 30 min, mainly owing to the synergistic effects of dispersion strengthening and second‐phase strengthening. The corrosion behavior was investigated by exposure in lead‐bismuth eutectic (LBE) at 550°C with dissolved oxygen concentration of 1 × 10 −6 wt.% for 500, 1000, 1500, and 2000 h. After exposure, the coating formed a compact Fe 3 O 4 ‐FeCr 2 O 4 ‐Al 2 O 3 triple‐layer oxide scale with a thickness of less than 1 μm, which was approximately one‐tenth of that formed on the substrate under the same conditions. The B2‐NiAl phase promoted the formation of the protective oxide scale, whereas the Laves phase suppressed its excessive growth. These results provide a mechanistic understanding and technical guidance for the design of protective materials for key moving parts in lead‐cooled fast reactors (LFRs).

title: Bidirectional Regulation of Tantalum Content on High‐Temperature Oxidation and Chloride Corrosion Resistance of CoCrFeNi High‐Entropy Alloys
abstract: ABSTRACT To address the trade‐off between high‐temperature oxidation resistance and chloride corrosion resistance of CoCrFeNi high‐entropy alloys (HEAs), CoCrFeNiTa x ( x = 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0) alloys were fabricated via vacuum hot‐pressing sintering. The bidirectional regulation of Ta content on oxidation at 800°C and corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution was systematically investigated. Increasing Ta degrades oxidation resistance with higher mass gain, parabolic rate constant K p , and thicker oxide layers, owing to the deteriorated oxide structure, diluted Cr‐based protective film, and accelerated ionic diffusion through the Laves phase. Conversely, Ta markedly improves corrosion resistance by raising the corrosion potential and reducing the corrosion current density, due to the formation of a dense Ta 2 O 5 passive film, which repairs structural defects and resists the attack of chloride ions. This work clarifies the underlying bidirectional regulation mechanisms and provides guidance for the composition design of HEAs applied in extreme environments.

title: PCFE‐Net: An Advanced Interpretable Model Fusing Feature Enhancement and Physical Monotonic Constraints for Predicting Corrosion Rates of Galvanized Steel in Extreme Typhoon and Non‐Typhoon Weather Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT Typhoons, as frequent extreme convective weather events, significantly affect regional environmental conditions and thus influence the atmospheric corrosion behavior of metallic materials. Yet, few studies examine corrosion mechanisms under typhoon conditions. This study focuses on the typhoon‐prone southeastern coast of China, using minute‐level Atmospheric Corrosion Monitor (ACM) sensor data to build a unified prediction framework for galvanized steel corrosion rates under both typhoon and normal conditions. We introduce five typhoon‐related variables: typhoon translation speed (Moving_ty), maximum wind speed near the typhoon center (Wind_ty), typhoon occurrence (Occur_ty), relative bearing between the typhoon direction and the corrosion site (Bearing_ty), and distance between the typhoon center and corrosion location (Distance_ty). We developed PCFE‐Net, a neural network combining feature enhancement and physical monotonic constraints, which significantly outperformed traditional machine learning methods. Predicted corrosion maps matched observed spatial patterns, and interpretability analyses confirmed the model aligns with established physical principles.

title: Machine Learning Approach for Corrosion Analysis in Copper–Stainless Steel Welds Produced by Cold Gas Tungsten Arc Welding
abstract: ABSTRACT The corrosion behavior of galvanically coupled copper–AISI 304 stainless‐steel welds (Cu‐Fe immiscible system) fabricated using the novel cold gas tungsten arc welding (CGTAW) process was investigated. The controlling factors and mechanisms governing corrosion in three types of anode‐dominated weld microstructures were discussed. In a contaminated circulating water environment, corrosion rates were associated with the degree of mixing between the Cu‐matrix and Fe‐based phases (uniform or over‐mixed distributions) and with the presence of defects. A hierarchical Random Forest (RF)‐based machine learning framework was developed to model the process–structure–property relationship, in which process parameters influence corrosion rate through intermediate microstructural evolution and defect formation.

title: Microbiologically Influenced Corrosion in an Oxidizing KMnO <sub>4</sub> Transfer Pipeline: Role of Biofilm‐Induced Anaerobic Microenvironments in Premature Failure
abstract: ABSTRACT In this study, Premature leakage of a stainless‐steel pipeline used to transfer a 4% potassium permanganate (KMnO 4 ) solution was investigated to identify the degradation mechanism responsible for the failure after a short service period. Visual inspection revealed tubercle formation and deposit accumulation on the inner pipe surface, while scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis showed localized corrosion features, including micro‐pitting and tunnel‐like cavities beneath biofilm layers. SEM‐EDS analysis detected sulfur‐rich corrosion products within the deposits and pit interiors, suggesting sulfide formation possibly associated with microbiologically influenced corrosion. The observed corrosion mechanism is consistent with microbial sulfate reduction coupled with electrochemical iron dissolution, leading to iron sulfide deposition and localized under‐deposit corrosion. The study demonstrates that biofilm formation can create localized anaerobic microenvironments that enable microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC), even in oxidizing KMnO 4 transfer systems, providing new insights into MIC risks in chemical‐handling pipelines.

title: Corrosion Behavior of Commercial FeCrAl and TiAl Alloys in Molten Pb With 2E‐7 wt% Oxygen at 600°C and 700°C
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid lead (Pb) is an attractive heat transfer fluid for advanced thermal energy storage (TES) systems. In the search for adequate structural materials that withstand the corrosive nature of liquid Pb at high temperature, Al‐containing materials might offer excellent corrosion resistance due to their ability to form protective alumina scales. This study investigates the corrosion behavior of two commercial ferritic FeCrAl alloys, Kanthal APM and Kanthal APMT, and two titanium aluminides, TNM‐B1 and GE 48‐2‐2, in liquid Pb under conditions relevant for TES systems. Exposure tests are performed in liquid Pb with 2E‐7 wt.% dissolved oxygen at 600°C and 700°C for up to 5000 h. Examination of the specimens after exposure shows the formation of stable and protective oxide scales at 600°C on all materials, while exposure at 700°C leads to various failure mechanisms, ranging from internal oxidation for APM to severe Pb penetration for TNM‐B1 and GE 48‐2‐2.

title: Corrosion Inhibition of S275 Carbon Steel in CO <sub>2</sub> Capture Systems Using Monoethanolamine (MEA) Solvent
abstract: ABSTRACT Corrosion in CO 2 capture units significantly impacts safety and costs. This study evaluates S275 carbon steel in CO 2 ‐loaded monoethanolamine (MEA) as a cost‐effective alternative to 316 L stainless steel, testing various inhibitors: methionine, imidazole, sodium sulfite, sodium metavanadate (NaVO 3 ), and copper(II) sulfate (CuSO 4 ). Corrosion performance is assessed using potentiodynamic polarization and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), while SEM and confocal microscopy analyze surface mechanisms. Results show that NaVO 3 and CuSO 4 provide the highest protection, reaching inhibition efficiencies of 94% (750 ppm) and 98% (1000 ppm), respectively. Polarization curves indicate that both inhibitors act as anodic inhibitors by forming protective layers. SEM confirm iron‐based oxides in NaVO 3 ‐treated samples and mixed copper–iron oxides in CuSO 4 ‐treated ones. Overall, S275 steel shows high potential for CO 2 capture systems when paired with effective inhibitors.

title: Corrosion Performance of Steel and Zinc‐Based Materials in Diverse Unsaturated Soils: Insights From a 2‐Year Field Exposure
abstract: ABSTRACT The corrosion of metals in soils is a major problem for asset managers within the infrastructure and energy sectors. Usually, the soil corrosivity class is defined using standards and field tests. In the context of solar park structures' durability, the present study was conducted for 2 years, in which the corrosion behavior of carbon steel, pure zinc, and hot‐dip galvanized steel was investigated through exposure to a variety of global unsaturated soil environments. Test sites included sandy and clay soils with varying pH levels and electrical resistivities. Corrosion was evaluated through visual inspection, mass‐loss measurements, and characterization of corrosion products using Raman and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy. Results highlight the critical influence of soil moisture, oxygen availability, resistivity, and sulfates on corrosion rates. Notably, the Fe/Zn corrosion rate ratio highlighted the material‐specific sensitivity to soil chemistry. Severe localized penetration and zinc coating consumption were observed in poorly‐drained saline sandy soil, challenging the predictive accuracy of the current DIN 50929 standard.

title: Inhibition of Temper Patch on Automotive Steel Coils by Nitrite‐Based Wet Temper Fluid
abstract: ABSTRACT This study evaluates the temper patch protection of a novel nitrite‐based wet temper fluid on three CRCA (cold rolled closed annealed) steel substrates: anodic cleaned, cathodic cleaned, and non‐ECL (electrolytic cleaning line). Findings indicate that anodic cleaning is the most effective, producing a uniform silicate layer coupled with nitrite ion adsorption leading to the highest charge transfer resistance ( R ct = 1.7 × 10 7 Ω), signifying exceptional corrosion resistance. In contrast, cathodic cleaning resulted in non‐uniform carbonaceous and silicate deposits, leading to the lowest R ct (2.8 × 10 5 Ω) and higher corrosion susceptibility. Scanning Kelvin probe studies confirmed more negative Volta potential for cathodic substrates, making them less noble. Raman spectroscopy identified protective iron oxides like hematite and goethite, which are more prevalent and stable on anodic substrates due to their low solubility products. Ultimately, the study concludes that anodic cleaning promotes a superior kinetic barrier at the metal‐electrolyte interface, offering robust protection against temper patch compared to cathodic and non‐ECL alternatives.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning Reveals Ni–Mo–Cu Synergistic Corrosion Behavior in Low‐Alloy Steels Under Simulated Marine Atmosphere
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the synergistic corrosion behavior of Ni, Mo, and Cu in the low‐alloy steel under simulated marine atmosphere by integrating interpretable machine learning (IML) with multiscale experimental validation. Results demonstrate that Transformer model can capture the complex, nonlinear, and time‐dependent corrosion behavior from a small−sample time‐series dataset, achieving high predictive accuracy and robust generalization in forecasting corrosion rates. IML analysis reveals that the synergistic corrosion resistance provided by Ni, Mo, and Cu is dynamically governed by their relative elemental concentrations, with Mo playing a critical regulatory role. When the Mo content exceeds both Ni and Cu, molybdenum oxides promote the formation of NiFe 2 O 4 and CuFeO 2 in higher proportions, which can enhance the rust layer's compactness and protectiveness. Conversely, insufficient Mo content leads to the dominance of the oxide phase associated with the most abundant element (Ni or Cu), suppressing the stable coexistence of other protective phases and thereby weakening the Ni–Mo–Cu synergistic effect, thus accelerating corrosion propagation.

title: Simultaneous Electrochemical and Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy Measurements on AA 7075
abstract: ABSTRACT This publication deals with the simultaneous acquisition of electrochemical and inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP‑OES) data. In a first approach, the authors use well‐known materials (Al (99.999%) and AA 7075) to validate the combination of both methods. Low‐millimolar sodium chloride solutions are used to evaluate the sensitivity of the combination, whereby the limits of detection and quantification must be considered, as well as the limited sample volume. Besides aluminum, the dissolution of the intermetallic phases, which are typical for the microstructure of AA 7075, was also monitored in terms of both time and potential. Under the selected operating conditions, corrosion rates and current densities were calculated based on ICP‐OES and compared with the electrochemically measured values.

title: Improved Corrosion Resistance of a Micro‐Alloyed Carbon Steel Assessed by Multi‐Element Electrical Resistance Probes and Coupons in Natural Seawater and Soil
abstract: ABSTRACT The corrosion behavior of two carbon steels, a conventional S355 GP and a newly developed micro‐alloyed grade (AMLoCor), was compared over 1 year in natural seawater and a corrosive soil using multi‐element electrical resistance (ER) probes and standard mass‐loss coupons. In both environments AMLoCor showed clearly improved uniform corrosion resistance, with reductions ranging from 25% in seawater to a factor of 2.4 in soil. Multi‐element ER probes provided real‐time corrosion kinetics and distribution information; average probe values agreed well with coupon mass‐loss data, particularly in soil. These results, obtained over 1 year of exposure, demonstrate the value of multi‐element ER monitoring for assessing and ranking the early‐stage corrosion performance of micro‐alloyed steels for piles and sheet piles in aggressive marine and soil environments, while highlighting that these short‐term rankings should not be directly extrapolated to long‐term service life.

title: Multi‐Method Investigation of Intergranular Corrosion of the Aluminium Alloy EN AW‐2024 With Different Cooling Rates After Solution Heat Treatment—Metallography and Eddy Current Testing
abstract: ABSTRACT Intergranular corrosion (IGC) of heat‐treatable aluminium (Al) alloys is generally attributed to the nature, frequency and distribution of intermetallic phases (IMPs). The time‐dependent hardening process is given specific focus. During this process, IMPs form within the supersaturated Al solid solution after solution annealing, cooling and aging. To date, only a few studies have investigated how cooling rate affects IGC susceptibility in 2xxx series alloys. Therefore, the EN AW‐2024 alloy was treated with various cooling rates after solution annealing, and its susceptibility to IGC and hardness were investigated using different methods. IGC depths from corrosion testing acc. to ISO 11846, as determined by light microscopy of cross‐sections, correlated very well with cooling rates and were consistent with both non‐destructive eddy current testing and changes in electrical conductivity. For practical corrosion testing as part of quality control, the non‐destructive eddy current method can provide valuable insights into the depth and extent of IGC of such a 2xxx series alloy. Whether this method can also be used for other aluminium alloy systems has to be investigated.

title: Formation and Failure of γ‐NiOOH During Nickel Corrosion in Oxygen‐Pressured Concentrated Alkali at 270°C
abstract: ABSTRACT The corrosion behavior of pure nickel in oxidizing concentrated alkaline environments was systematically studied. Weight‐loss measurements and surface/phase characterization show that nickel deviates from conventional passivation, in which a continuous, adherent NiO/Ni(OH) 2 film suppresses further dissolution. In 75 wt% NaOH at 270°C under 4.2 MPa oxygen pressure, nickel undergoes rapid and persistent dissolution, with a weight‐loss‐derived corrosion rate reaching 6.088 ± 0.16 mm y −1 at 168 h (mean ± SD, n = 3). SEM, XRD, Raman, and XPS identify only a thin, poorly crystalline Ni(OH) 2 ‐like layer on the specimen surface, with no thick, continuous, adherent protective film. In contrast, the flake‐like solids collected from the autoclave are identified as γ‐NiOOH by XRD and Raman. This spatial separation suggests that Ni(OH) 2 is further oxidized to γ‐NiOOH under high O 2 pressure and detaches as loosely flakes, continuously exposing fresh metallic nickel surface. The inability to establish a stable, protective scale explains the sustained high corrosion rate and highlights the limitations of γ‐NiOOH as a corrosion product under strongly oxidizing, concentrated alkaline conditions.

title: Cold Gas Sprayed Titanium Coating for Corrosion Protection of Bipolar Plates in Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Climate‐neutral green hydrogen is produced by water electrolysis powered through renewable energy. In next generation electrolyzer, like the proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE), steel‐based bipolar plates (BPP) are supposed to replace titanium BPPs in order to minimize manufacturing costs. Yet, corrosion of steel is a possible threat to this next‐generation design. Consequently, corrosion protection coatings for the steel‐based BPPs are currently developed. In a novel approach, cold gas spraying (CGS) is used to apply a corrosion protection titanium coating on a BPP made of X2CrNiMo17‐12‐2 with a thickness of d = 0.5 mm. The coating is characterized through structural analysis methods and also in short‐term corrosion tests. The short‐term corrosion test shows high corrosion protection. The results demonstrate a new promising coating concept for corrosion protection for steel‐based BPPs in PEMWE. In this study, corrosion properties of cold gassprayed titanium coatings are evaluated for the first time regarding PEMWE requirements.

title: Mechanistic Insights Into Atmospheric Corrosion Behaviour of Interstitial‐Free Steel Under Tropical Marine Climate of Mumbai
abstract: ABSTRACT The formation of a protective rust layer on the surface of the steel slows down the corrosion process. In the present study, the atmospheric corrosion behaviour of the interstitial free (IF) steel coupons was investigated by exposing the coupons in the atmosphere of Mumbai for 1 year. The electrochemical properties of the rust layer were studied using open circuit potential (OCP), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and Mott‐Schottky (MS) analyses. Grazing index X‐ray diffraction, scanning electron microscope and Raman spectroscopy determined the rust layer morphology and phases. The results depicted that the development of the rust layer is strongly dependent on the environmental parameters and pollutant levels in the atmosphere. High accumulated rainfall and high pollutant levels resulted in a nonprotective rust layer. The physical representation of the rust layer evolution in the atmosphere of Mumbai was elucidated based on the rust layer characterisations, EIS, and MS results.

title: Development and Validation of Corrosion Behavior Models for T91 Materials With Different Bismuth Contents and Oxygen Concentrations
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper proposes a physically based double‐layer oxide film growth model for T91 ferritic–martensitic steel in lead–bismuth eutectic (LBE). It describes the growth and evolution of oxide scales under varying bismuth contents and dissolved oxygen concentrations, using mass transport and thermodynamics with numerical solutions via the Brent algorithm. Validated against static corrosion experiments, the model uniquely incorporates bismuth content via composition‐dependent solubility of oxygen and iron. Compared with existing LBE corrosion models, it shows reasonable accuracy in predicting oxide layer thicknesses. The model reproduces magnetite and Fe–Cr spinel growth, as well as the transition from oxidation to dissolution corrosion under low‐oxygen conditions, offering a theoretical reference for material reliability assessment in lead‐bismuth‐cooled fast reactors.

title: Superhydrophobic Coating on 2A97‐T3 Al‐Li Alloy via HCl/FAS‐17: Fabrication and Corrosion Resistance
abstract: ABSTRACT The 2A97 Al‐Li alloy is widely utilized in aerospace because of its excellent mechanical properties. However, when the alloy is exposed to a moist climate, its service life is seriously affected by surface corrosion. To address the issue, a superhydrophobic surface with enhanced corrosion resistance was successfully developed on the 2A97‐T3 Al‐Li alloy by constructing HCl/FAS composite structures. The alloy was etched in a 5 mol/L HCl solution for 8 min, and then it was immersed in boiling water for 30 min. Finally, the alloy was soaked in a 0.1 mol/L perfluorodecyltriethoxysilane (FAS‐17) solution for 2 h. The low‐adhesion coating of a water contact angle was 152.7°, and the rolling angle was 5.64°. The corrosion resistance of the modified alloy was significantly improved compared to the original alloy. Specifically, the corrosion potential increased from −0.732 to −0.408 V, and the corrosion rate decreased dramatically from 3.322 × 10 −8 to 3.917 × 10 −9 A/cm 2 . The surface activity of the 2A97 Al‐Li alloy was reduced by these modifications. An innovative and effective method was provided to improve the corrosion resistance of the Al‐Li alloy. It holds significant promise for extending the service life of Al‐Li alloys in moisture‐prone environments.
